newsitem.title: USA: Florida increases funding for bullet train.
newsitem.headline: Florida increases funding for bullet train.

text.p: The Florida Department of Transportation has tripled its tentative financial commitment to the proposed high-speed rail system to $6.5 billion, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said Wednesday.
The money would be paid over 40 years, starting at $70 million and increasing 4 percent annually.

The transportation department had originally pledged $2.1 billion over 30 years for the train system linking Miami, Orlando and Tampa. The money would come from a transportation trust fund financed largely by gas taxes.
The newspaper said the price increase was buried in the fine print of a 37-page contract announced last month with the project's private partner, Florida Overland eXpress, or FOX.
Legislators were unaware of the price increase until state Transportation Secretary Ben Watts testified about the project Tuesday before the Senate Finance Committee.
Watts said he did not know why the higher payment was not publicly disclosed, but said it was necessary to build the unprecedented project.
FOX's cash committmenet would be much less, about $350 million, but a lot of that money would be advanced earlier in the project than previously proposed.
Trains would travel along the 325-mile tracks at 125 to 200 mph.

The state is still seeking a federal guarantee for the project's bonds. The governor and Cabinet would have to give final approval in late 1999 or early 2000 for the project to proceed and the Legislature would then have to approve annual appropriations for the state's contribution.

The FOX consortium includes nearly 30 companies led by Fluor Daniel Inc, a unit of Fluor Corp, Bombardier Inc, GEC Alsthom Transport S.A., and Odebrecht Contractors of Florida, a unit of Odebrecht S.A..
